# Structural Time-Series Modeling and Daily Primary Production (EP model)

**Author:** Willem Stolte (with Copilot)\
**Date:** 2026-03-03 (Europe/Amsterdam)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Objective

Build structural time‑series models for key photosynthesis parameters (**PBmax, alpha, Eopt, Kd, Chl_surface**) per compartment, predict their daily values, and compute **depth‑integrated daily primary production** (PP) using the **Eilers & Peeters (1988)** P–E model with photoinhibition. Predictions are driven by **daily incident PAR** derived from KNMI global radiation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Inputs, units, and conventions

- **pp_wide.csv** – sporadic measurements per *compartiment* with columns:
  - `PBmax_EP` (mg C (mg Chl‑a)⁻¹ h⁻¹), `alfaB_EP` (mg C (mg Chl‑a)⁻¹ h⁻¹ per (µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹)⁻¹), `Eopt_EP` (µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹), `Kd` (m⁻¹), `chl_surface` (µg L⁻¹ ≡ mg m⁻³), optional `bottomdepth` (m), `irradiance_J_cm2` (J cm⁻² d⁻¹).
- **knmi_daily.csv** – daily global short‑wave **Q** in **J cm⁻² d⁻¹** with station id `STN`.
- Unit convention: 1 µg L⁻¹ Chl‑a = 1 mg m⁻³.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Incident PAR from KNMI global radiation

KNMI provides global short‑wave radiation **Q** as energy per area per day (J cm⁻² d⁻¹). Plants respond to **PAR** (400–700 nm) quantified as photon flux. We convert global radiation to **PPFD** (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) and **DLI** (mol m⁻² d⁻¹) using the widely adopted relation

$$ \text{PPFD} \;\approx\; R_g \times f_{\text{PAR}} \times c_{J\to\mu mol},$$

where $R_g$ is mean irradiance in W m⁻² (= J m⁻² s⁻¹), $f_{\text{PAR}}$ is the PAR fraction (typ. 0.45–0.50), and $c_{J\to\mu mol}$ is the energy‑to‑quanta factor (default **4.6 µmol J⁻¹**). This is documented in the `bigleaf::Rg.to.PPFD` function and vignette. [1](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/bigleaf/html/Rg.to.PPFD.html)[2](https://rdrr.io/cran/bigleaf/man/Rg.to.PPFD.html)

Given KNMI’s daily sum **Q** (J cm⁻² d⁻¹):

1.  Convert to J m⁻² d⁻¹: $J_{m^2,day} = Q \times 10^4$.
2.  Mean over 24h: $\overline{R_g} = J_{m^2,day}/86400$ W m⁻².
3.  24‑h mean **PPFD**: $\text{PPFD}_{24h} = \overline{R_g} \cdot f_{PAR} \cdot 4.6$ (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹).
4.  **DLI**: $\text{DLI} = \text{PPFD}_{24h} \times 86400/10^6$ (mol m⁻² d⁻¹).

We also compute a **daylight‑mean PPFD** by dividing the DLI by astronomical daylength (hours from a solar‑geometry approximation) when integrating only during daylight. In this project we use **f_PAR = 0.45** and integrate over **daylength (not 24 h)** as requested. [1](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/bigleaf/html/Rg.to.PPFD.html)[2](https://rdrr.io/cran/bigleaf/man/Rg.to.PPFD.html)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Structural time‑series model per compartment

For each parameter $\theta \in \{P_{B\max},\,\alpha,\,E_{opt},\,K_d,\,\text{Chl}\}$, and for each `compartiment`, we fit a **structural regression** with:

- **Seasonal cycle** via Fourier terms of order *K* with period 365 d (captures annual periodicity).
- **Long‑term trend** via a natural spline $ns(t)$ (captures multi‑year drift/eutrophication/climate shifts).
- **Spring bloom dynamics** via a set of **Gaussian basis functions** centred around DOY \~70–115 (width \~10 d) to represent the typical rapid March bloom.

This is implemented in **tidymodels** as a **workflow** (recipe + linear model), fitted **per compartment**. It is a transparent, regularized alternative to a full state‑space filter and is easy to tune (K and df) and diagnose.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Eilers & Peeters (1988) P–E curve with photoinhibition

We compute mass‑specific photosynthesis $P(E)$ from incident irradiance $E$ (µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹) using the Eilers & Peeters steady‑state curve including photoinhibition:

$$ P(E) = \frac{E}{\tfrac{E^2}{\alpha E_{opt}^2} + \tfrac{E}{P_{B\max}} - \tfrac{2E}{\alpha E_{opt}} + \tfrac{1}{\alpha}}.$$

This parameterization ($\alpha, E_{opt}, P_{B\max}$) is standard and documented in the `phytotools::fitEP` manual/help, which reproduces the EP model in this exact algebraic form. [3](https://rdrr.io/cran/phytotools/man/fitEP.html)[4](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/phytotools/versions/1.0/topics/fitEP)[5](https://github.com/cran/phytotools/blob/master/man/fitEP.Rd)

- $\alpha$: initial slope at low light.
- $E_{opt}$: optimum light where $P$ peaks.
- $P_{B\max}$: maximum mass‑specific rate.

Units are consistent with your inputs: $P(E)$ returns **mg C (mg Chl‑a)⁻¹ h⁻¹** for given $E$.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Depth integration and daily PP

Assuming exponential light attenuation and vertically uniform chlorophyll (well‑mixed layer), irradiance at depth $z$ is $E(z) = E_0\,e^{-K_d z}$. The depth‑integrated **areal** production for a day is

$$ PP_{daily} = \left[\int_0^{Z} P(E_0 e^{-K_d z})\,\text{Chl}\;\mathrm{d}z\right] \times h_{day},$$

with $Z$ (bottom depth), $h_{day}$ (hours integrated; here daylength). The integral is computed numerically per day with the predicted parameters and the day’s $E_0$ (PPFD). If vertical chlorophyll structure is available later, replace $\text{Chl}$ by $\text{Chl}(z)$ in the integrand.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Prediction workflow (daily)

1.  **From KNMI Q → PAR**: compute **PPFD_daylight** (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) and **hours_day**.
2.  **Predict parameters** per compartment & date using the structural models.
3.  **Compute PP**: for each date and compartment, evaluate EP at depth‑attenuated light and integrate over depth 0→Z and time 0→hours_day.
4.  **Outputs**: `daily_PP_predictions.csv` (per day), `annual_summaries.csv` (annual sums), and per‑compartment plots.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. Diagnostics

For each parameter × compartment we save: - **Fit statistics**: RMSE, MAE, R² on the training data (and CV if configured). - **Predicted vs observed** scatter with 1:1 line. - **Residual time‑series** and seasonal residual checks.

The modeling choices (K for Fourier, df for trend, bloom timing) can be tuned via time‑series resampling; the provided defaults work robustly for typical temperate seasonality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 9. Assumptions and sensitivity

- **PAR conversion**: we use $f_{PAR}=0.45$ and $4.6\,\mu mol\,J^{-1}$. Literature/practice commonly uses 0.45–0.50 and 4.6; differences in DLI are (\~10%). If local calibration exists, override in config. [1](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/bigleaf/html/Rg.to.PPFD.html)[2](https://rdrr.io/cran/bigleaf/man/Rg.to.PPFD.html)
- **Daylength vs 24 h**: we integrate during **daylight hours**, computing a daylight‑mean PPFD from DLI/Daylength (astronomical daylength approximation). This better matches diurnal forcing than a 24‑h average.
- **Vertical homogeneity**: assumes **well‑mixed** water column; if stratified or if deep chlorophyll maxima are present, PP may be biased.
- **No temperature/nutrients**: EP parameters are modeled from season/trend/bloom structure only. If temperature or nutrients are available, they can enter as covariates.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 10. References

- Eilers & Peeters parametric form and usage: `phytotools::fitEP` documentation ([rdrr.io](https://rdrr.io/cran/phytotools/man/fitEP.html)) and RDocumentation mirror. [3](https://rdrr.io/cran/phytotools/man/fitEP.html)[4](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/phytotools/versions/1.0/topics/fitEP)
- Algebraic EP form ($\alpha, E_{opt}, P_{B\max}$) also shown in GitHub mirror of CRAN man page. [5](https://github.com/cran/phytotools/blob/master/man/fitEP.Rd)
- Global radiation → PAR conversions (PPFD, DLI) and factors ($f_{PAR}, 4.6\,\mu mol\,J^{-1}$): `bigleaf::Rg.to.PPFD` documentation. [1](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/bigleaf/html/Rg.to.PPFD.html)[2](https://rdrr.io/cran/bigleaf/man/Rg.to.PPFD.html)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 11. Reproducibility

- Implemented in **tidyverse + tidymodels**.
- Configuration collected at top of the script for easy changes (PAR factors, daylength integration, seasonal/trend complexity).
- Outputs written to `output/` with deterministic code paths.
